Audience: every first-time Wisconsin Class D applicant, and especially teen drivers, whom the handbook warns face doubled crash risk with a teen passenger.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the chapter teaches the stop, turn or speed-up choices and ABS braking [A01], the after-crash duties and when police must be told [A02], and what to do when brakes, tires, engine, headlights or the gas pedal fail [A03].
Level: branching procedures plus two dollar thresholds; moderate load with several opposite-action pairs.
Prerequisites: the driving conditions section on skids and braking, and the basics sections on space and stopping.
